_notes: This example ships no docker-compose.yml, so the smoke runner
(which gates on a compose file) does not pick it up. The reason is
the build, not the stack: settlement lives behind cargo features
and Dockerfile.cloudbuild builds the default set, so the image the
other examples use would start this config and fail on the
configured rail's missing feature. Build the binary with
--features payment-lightning-cln and run fixture.py beside it, as
The four cases above are the order-independent half of the
contract, true at any point in a run. The paid path is not
expressible here because it needs an out-of-band payment between
two requests; bin/settle-once.sh runs that sequence and prints the
origin's own hit counter after each step.
The same five outcomes are asserted automatically by
e2e/tests/settlement_gate.rs, which stands up the same stub node
and the same counting origin in Rust.
